_comment: Which weaknesses can arise in which languages, so coverage density means
something. Measured against every possible cell, density understates the
corpus badly: use-after-free in Java and XXE in C are not gaps anyone
Each entry lists the languages where the weakness is reachable and
idiomatic. `reason` explains the exclusions and is required whenever any
language is left out — an exclusion nobody can check is an assertion, not
a fact. The map is validated against the answer key in CI: a tier-1 case
existing for a pair listed as inapplicable fails the build, because one of
the two is wrong and silently trusting either is worse.
Language set: java kotlin python javascript typescript go csharp c cpp

CWE-22.name: path traversal
CWE-22.reason: Every language here opens files by path.

CWE-59.name: link following
CWE-59.reason: Requires resolving a filesystem path that may be a symbolic link; every language here opens files by path.

CWE-74.name: injection
CWE-74.reason: The injection parent class. Any language that passes data into an interpreter can be reported at this level when a tool declines to commit to a child.

CWE-77.name: command injection
CWE-77.reason: As CWE-78; the distinction is the layer, not the language.

CWE-78.name: OS command injection
CWE-78.reason: Every language here can start a process.

CWE-79.name: cross-site scripting
CWE-79.reason: Requires emitting markup to a browser. C and C++ do not serve HTML in any idiom this corpus would be testing.

CWE-88.name: argument injection
CWE-88.reason: Any language that builds a command line can put an attacker-controlled value where the callee expects a flag.

CWE-89.name: SQL injection
CWE-89.reason: Anything with a database driver can build a statement by concatenation.

CWE-94.name: code injection
CWE-94.reason: Requires runtime evaluation of source. Go, Rust, C, C++ and Swift compile ahead of time with no eval.

CWE-116.name: improper encoding or escaping of output

CWE-120.name: buffer copy without size check
CWE-120.reason: Requires an unchecked copy into a fixed buffer; managed languages have no such primitive.

CWE-121.name: stack-based buffer overflow
CWE-121.reason: Requires stack-allocated buffers under manual control.

CWE-125.name: out-of-bounds read
CWE-125.reason: Requires reading past an allocation without a runtime bound check. Managed languages raise instead; Rust reaches it only inside `unsafe`.

CWE-134.name: externally controlled format string
CWE-134.reason: Requires a variadic format function that reads the format at runtime. Rust's format strings are compile-time checked; managed languages do not expose %n-style writes.

CWE-190.name: integer overflow or wraparound
CWE-190.reason: Requires fixed-width integers that wrap. Python integers are arbitrary-precision, and JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP and Ruby promote or use doubles rather than wrapping.

CWE-269.name: improper privilege management
CWE-269.reason: Privilege is an application concept, not a language feature.

CWE-307.name: improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts

CWE-312.name: cleartext storage of sensitive information
CWE-312.reason: Any language can write a secret to disk or a database without encrypting it.

CWE-327.name: broken crypto
CWE-327.reason: Every language here can reach a weak digest or cipher.

CWE-345.name: insufficient verification of data authenticity
CWE-345.reason: Any language can accept data without checking the signature or provenance it claims.

CWE-352.name: cross-site request forgery
CWE-352.reason: A property of web frameworks handling state-changing requests; not reachable in C or C++ as used here.

CWE-384.name: session fixation
CWE-384.reason: Needs a session the caller can influence before authenticating, so it follows the web frameworks rather than the language. C and C++ host web servers but not idiomatically in this corpus.

CWE-416.name: use after free
CWE-416.reason: Requires manual lifetime management. Garbage-collected and reference-counted languages cannot reach a freed object; Rust reaches it only inside `unsafe`.

CWE-434.name: unrestricted upload of dangerous file type
CWE-434.reason: Requires an HTTP upload handler; excluded for C and C++ for the same reason as XSS.

CWE-444.name: inconsistent interpretation of HTTP requests
CWE-444.reason: Request smuggling needs an HTTP parser in front of or inside the application; the same reasoning as session fixation.

CWE-471.name: modification of assumed-immutable data
CWE-471.reason: Prototype and attribute pollution need a runtime whose object model is mutable at the language level. Compiled and statically-dispatched languages have no equivalent.

CWE-476.name: NULL pointer dereference
CWE-476.reason: Needs a null-valued reference that is dereferenced. Included for managed languages where it is a real defect class (NullPointerException, NullReferenceException, nil map/pointer). Excluded for Python, Ruby, PHP and JavaScript, where the analogous error is an attribute error on None/nil rather than a null dereference, and for Rust, whose Option type makes it unrepresentable in safe code.

CWE-502.name: unsafe deserialisation
CWE-502.reason: Requires a deserialiser that reconstructs arbitrary objects and invokes their hooks. C, C++ and Rust have no such facility in the standard library.

CWE-532.name: sensitive information in a log file

CWE-601.name: open redirect
CWE-601.reason: Requires an HTTP redirect built from a caller-supplied target; not reachable in C or C++ as used here.

CWE-610.name: externally controlled reference to a resource in another sphere
CWE-610.reason: The parent of SSRF and several file-reference weaknesses, reachable in any language.

CWE-611.name: XML external entity
CWE-611.reason: Requires an XML parser that resolves external entities by default. Rust's parsers do not; C and C++ reach it only through libxml2, which is out of scope here.

CWE-613.name: insufficient session expiration
CWE-613.reason: A session that outlives its welcome is a web-session property, so it follows the frameworks.

CWE-668.name: exposure of resource to wrong sphere
CWE-668.reason: A broad parent class covering files, sockets and memory handed to the wrong caller.

CWE-732.name: incorrect permission assignment for critical resource
CWE-732.reason: Any language that creates a file or directory can create it world-writable.

CWE-787.name: out-of-bounds write
CWE-787.reason: As CWE-125, in the write direction.

CWE-798.name: hard-coded credentials
CWE-798.reason: A literal in source is possible in every language.

CWE-918.name: server-side request forgery
CWE-918.reason: Needs an HTTP client taking a caller-supplied URL. C and C++ can do this via libcurl but it is not where this weakness is tested.

CWE-1395.name: dependency on a vulnerable component
CWE-1395.reason: Every language here has a package manager and a manifest.
